I have never been a Moderator on Reddit or Voat, and I plan on never, ever becoming one. But I occasionally see stupid shit about moderators on both sites - i.e. Mods ban a user and get really snarky or passive-aggressive about why they did it, and get all uppity about it, and usually with no good reason for having banned the user to begin with. This shit bothers me quite a bit, and so I just had an idea:

I'm just spit-balling here.

What if, before banning a user, all Mods should be obligated to post proof that they have attempted to use rational communication to resolve any problems they might have with users, and **only** be allowed to ban somebody if that user is refusing to communicate rationally, if the user is lying to the mod, or if said user is still creating problems after a warning, etc.

Maybe create a public 'side room' in each subverse that has a chronological history of each banned user, attached with all the communications that user had with the Mods at the time of his ban; then, if a Mod is shown to have unjustly banned somebody, the other mods are obligated to overturn the ban. If a mod is found to have banned users unjustly too many times (some arbitrary amount of bans over some arbitrary length of time), then he should be removed on the grounds of 'abuse of power'. If a ban is found to be unjust, the Mod that banned the user , as well as any Mods that refused to overturn it, are given a permanent 'negative mark' and can be removed if they gather enough marks.

Is any of this possible at all? Is any of this even a good idea? Despite all the Mod abuse that has taken place in the past, I don't think it would be just to create an environment wherein all Mods are automatically treated like criminals to be kept under a microscope all the time.
